spec.cue: The view looks out in every direction at once, and it is dim, with a blue-green tint and a faint glow where things move.

field.name: squeeze
field.note: the whole picture squeezed around the animal, as the records give a full 360 degree view

haptic.name: buzz
haptic.note: a short vibration where the browser can vibrate, and a pulse at the picture's edge where it cannot

rows: A scorpion's median and lateral eyes together look in every direction around it, so the picture wraps all the way round.
Scorpion eyes are most sensitive to green and blue-green light, with a smaller peak in the ultraviolet, so the picture has a faint blue-green tint.
Scorpions are nocturnal, and their eyes respond to starlight levels of light, so the picture is brightened to show what the animal can make out at night.
No record gives how sharp a scorpion's view is. This view assumes coarse shapes and light, a faint colour, and a brighter picture. The knock buzz and the edge pulse are the app's.
Vibrations through the sand, the touch of the legs, and the air movements sensed by hairs on the pedipalps are not shown.

claims.how: Both records give a 360 degree field of view for scorpions, and the picture is set to that value.

quotes.quote: scorpions can apparently see 360° around their body
Together, the two eyes have a 360 deg field of view
